I went ahead and prototyped this. The implementation is up on the [`vscode-integration`](https://github.com/wagner-sousa/opencode/tree/vscode-integration) branch:

- **`GET /v1/models`** — lists every model as `providerID/modelID`
- **`POST /v1/chat/completions`** — streaming (SSE) and non-streaming, tools pass through to the client so VSCode owns execution
- **`GET /v1/vscode-config`** — returns a ready-to-use `chatLanguageModels.json`

Auth via Bearer token (`OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD`); `/v1/models` and `/v1/vscode-config` are public. A `--vscode` flag pins port 4096, generates a token, and prints the setup steps.

The core idea: requests go straight to the model through the AI SDK — the agent loop doesn't run. The client handles tool execution, opencode just acts as a local gateway.

The main files:

- [groups/gateway.ts](https://github.com/wagner-sousa/opencode/blob/vscode-integration/packages/opencode/src/server/routes/instance/httpapi/groups/gateway.ts) — endpoint declarations
- [handlers/gateway.ts](https://github.com/wagner-sousa/opencode/blob/vscode-integration/packages/opencode/src/server/routes/instance/httpapi/handlers/gateway.ts) — request handling and streaming
- [gateway/openai-convert.ts](https://github.com/wagner-sousa/opencode/blob/vscode-integration/packages/opencode/src/server/routes/instance/httpapi/gateway/openai-convert.ts) — pure OpenAI ↔ AI SDK conversion (unit-tested)
- [gateway/auth.ts](https://github.com/wagner-sousa/opencode/blob/vscode-integration/packages/opencode/src/server/routes/instance/httpapi/gateway/auth.ts) — Bearer auth
- [openai-convert.test.ts](https://github.com/wagner-sousa/opencode/blob/vscode-integration/packages/opencode/test/server/gateway/openai-convert.test.ts) — ~170 lines of tests
- [README](https://github.com/wagner-sousa/opencode/blob/vscode-integration/packages/opencode/src/server/routes/instance/httpapi/gateway/README.md) — usage docs

This issue might be a duplicate of existing issues. Please check:
- #21636: GitHub Action commits unrelated dirty working tree changes (no way to disable auto-commit) — same root cause: the Action auto-commits dirty state that was not produced by the agent, and there is no way to disable this behavior.

Thanks, #21636 is the same underlying safety problem: the Action treats any dirty worktree as commit intent.

This issue adds a narrower reproduction where the dirty state is not created by a user workflow step before OpenCode. It can be created by the OpenCode GitHub Action flow itself:

1. The workflow checks out the repository with recursive submodules.
2. The Action later checks out the PR branch.
3. The Action does not run `git submodule update --init --recursive` after that checkout.
4. For a submodule-only PR, the submodule worktree can now appear dirty.
5. The agent may make no edits, but the Action still commits and pushes because `git status --porcelain` is non-empty.

So I agree this belongs to the same design problem as #21636, but the submodule case is important because it can happen even without an explicit pre-OpenCode mutation step in the workflow.

The broader fix requested in #21636, such as a no-write/comment-only mode or explicit commit intent contract, would solve this too. A narrower mitigation would be synchronizing submodules after the Action checks out the PR branch, but that does not replace the need for an explicit auto-commit control.

OpenCode preserves MCP server and tool-name casing when registering tools. The lowercase name shown in the error was emitted by the model/provider; OpenCode did not lowercase the registered name during dispatch.
Accidental creation during permission testing. Closing.

OpenCode preserves MCP tool names and uses the same registered tool-map key for structured provider tool exposure and dispatch. It does not inject a second, underscore-normalized set of MCP tools into the system prompt. Likewise, OpenCode does not lowercase capitalized MCP names before dispatch; the lowercase name in #31506 was emitted by the model or provider.

MCP tool names are case-sensitive, and case-insensitive or -/_-insensitive matching can become ambiguous when a server legitimately exposes distinct names such as Get/get or get-item/get_item.

Root cause analysis by Gemini:

1. Large Data File: When `opencode` starts, it reads a very large list of AI models (over 2 megabytes) from the cache file `models.json`. If this file is missing, it downloads the exact same large list from the internet instead.
2. Optimization Crash: To read this large file quickly, the application runtime tries to speed up execution by compiling the instructions on the fly.
3. Security Guard Trigger: Apple Silicon Mac computers have a built-in security feature that checks every compiled instruction to ensure it has not been tampered with. Because of a bug in the runtime's compiler on macOS, this security check fails when compiling the code to process the massive models list, causing the computer to immediately halt the application (a trace trap) to protect itself.

Opened PR #32089 to fix this. The root cause was two bugs in processor.ts: the doom loop check only searched within the current assistant message (not the full session), and it did slice(-3) before filtering, so any text/reasoning parts in the tail would cause the check to silently pass. Fix uses filterCompactedEffect to search all messages and filters first before counting.
